requirement: ADR-0010 personal-project scope, one representative emulator smoke set, consolidated fixtures, and Tracker reference host are authoritative.
All production toolchains and third-party sources are pinned, integrity-checked, licensed, and reproducible enough to rebuild on the pinned runner.
Only generated bounded privacy-classified event/value types can record; prohibited and unknown fields are rejected.
Kotlin, C, and Rust public contracts are versioned, bounded, panic-safe, and compatibility-tested.
Process, segment, artifact, summary, build, R8, ELF, and OS-correlation identities use one exact persist-before-use and match-before-symbolication contract.
Install, readiness, bounded queues, local policy gates, and explicit degraded/closed outcomes are implemented without an implicit recording opt-in.
One UID-wide hard bound accounts for ordinary data, raw artifacts, summaries, journals, indexes, staging, temporary files, file counts, and compaction workspace.
Direct Boot admits generated C0 only and coordinates fail-closed pending/active deny state with CE policy; live repetition is optional for Tracker.

ALL_TRACEBOX_DATA commits a durable CE/DE deny, quiesces writers and the handler, marks owned roots ineligible, and clears all accessible in-scope ordinary, raw, summary, tombstone, snapshot, journal, index, staging, and DE diagnostic state before reporting success. Per-record/summary selective deletion is optional post-foundation work and is not exposed.
One private capture-only handler uses bounded local IPC, peer checks, finite retries/timeouts, socket death notification, no polling, and no uploader.
Crashpad capture journals identity/origin/epoch before bytes, enforces C2 quarantine/quota/TTL, derives an ID-free structural summary, and deletes unverifiable orphans.
The async-signal-safe emergency fallback is initialized, ingested once after restart, policy-gated, bounded, and exactly chained when Crashpad is unavailable; live repetition is optional for Tracker.

JVM and Rust capture are bounded, structurally exclude messages, contain recursion/panics, persist through the shared policy/storage path, and chain prior handlers exactly once; the representative emulator set exercises JVM capture while Rust remains host-validated.
The live watchdog is lifecycle-aware and bounded, never claims confirmation alone, and ApplicationExitInfo import is token/policy-gated, crash-safe, idempotent, and tombstone-exact.
Snapshot transformation strips internal identities, raw Standard export is forbidden, deterministic CBOR/ZIP bytes are bounded, and preview bytes equal approved bytes.
Only the Tracebox disclosure UI can create an opaque digest-bound approval; save/share use finalized bytes and report only observable outcomes.
The offline CLI validates before allocation and retraces/symbolicates only with exact R8/ELF/Rust identity matches while retaining unresolved raw frames.
Production manifests, dependency closures, DEX references, native imports, and CLI graph contain no Tracebox networking surface; required emulator smoke paths make no observed attempt.
The consolidated fixture retains the full stable diagnostic inventory, while the manifest names the representative scenarios required for this personal release.
Hard architectural bounds are host-tested; startup time and PSS may be observed once, while CPU/wakeup, percentile, battery, and package-memory campaigns are advisory.
One final release-diff review fixes blocker, critical, and major findings; additional subsystem or external certification rounds are optional.

Host integration is prepared after IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLETE, then an immutable PERSONAL_RELEASE_READY candidate integrates into Tracker-Android's normal application with generated events, Standard Diagnostics as the first-install default plus persisted user controls, sole JVM/native/Rust crash and logging ownership, separate exit-history responsibilities, combined deletion reporting, and legacy stores retained only for bounded read/export/delete migration.
AEAD, age/X25519, per-record/summary selective deletion, metrics/traces, desktop UI, API 37.1 adapters, and advanced profiling are outside the personal foundation release.
